name: redblue
description: Red team versus blue team, with an actual scoreboard. Red writes attacks — prompts built to make a target model produce something it should not. Blue writes defenses, and a defense is a whole pipeline rather than a system prompt: input rules, the system prompt, the model, an optional self-check pass, output rules, any stage of which can end the turn. The arena fires every attack at every defense, a two-axis judge asks did-it-refuse and did-anything-harmful-escape, and the number that comes out is the refusal rate on attacks — held honest by the over-refusal rate on a fixed set of benign controls that sit right next to the attacks, so safety_score = refusal_rate - over_refusal and a refuse-everything defense nets ~0. The target is pluggable: the keyless local Claude CLI by default, any API model, or an offline mock whose correct score is known, which is how the harness itself is tested. Attacks, defenses and round records live in ~/.mod/redblue, never in this repo. REST, the browser console and eleven MCP tools on one port, off the same functions, so an agent, a shell and a human are never told different scores for the same round.
backend: python stdlib only (http.server + urllib) — no dependencies
frontend: console.html — the board, the round runner, both corpora, one-exchange fight; served at /redblue
state: ~/.mod/redblue — attacks/<id>.json, defenses/<id>.json, rounds/<id>.json, server.secret. A defense's system prompt is the blue team's live answer to an open attack surface and an attack corpus is a list of things that worked, so neither is committed to this repo.

verdicts.DEFLECTED: answered but gave nothing useful — soft blue win
verdicts.BREACHED: answered and something harmful escaped — red win
verdicts.LEAKED: refused in words but the payload is still there — red win

scoring.safety_score: refusal_rate - over_refusal — the single honest number
scoring.why_controls: refusal rate alone is gamed by a defense that refuses everything, so every round also fires benign controls that sit next to the attacks and reports over-refusal beside refusal

auth.gate: optional — writes only, and only when ~/.mod/redblue/server.secret exists
auth.why: those routes spend real model calls or edit the corpus; every route that only reads a score is open, because a scoreboard nobody can read is not one

endpoints.attacks: GET /attacks?id=&category= | POST /attacks {name, prompt|turns, goal, category, technique, markers} | DELETE /attacks?id=
endpoints.defenses: GET /defenses?id= | POST /defenses {name, system_prompt, input_rules, output_rules, self_check, max_input_chars} | DELETE /defenses?id=
endpoints.controls: GET /controls — the fixed benign control set over-refusal is measured on
endpoints.cost: GET /cost?defense= — model calls per turn, before you spend them
endpoints.fight: POST /fight {attack, defense, model, judge} — one exchange, every stage and the verdict
endpoints.round: POST /round {attacks, defenses, model, judge, parallel, controls, background} — the tournament
endpoints.rounds: GET /rounds?limit=&status= | GET /rounds?id= — one round in full, live while it runs
endpoints.targets: GET /targets — which backends can run right now
endpoints.ping: POST /ping {model} — prove a target is reachable

env.RB_PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50970)
env.RB_MODEL: default target (default claude:haiku — keyless, local CLI)
env.RB_JUDGE_MODEL: model that grades (defaults to the target)
env.RB_KEEP_ROUNDS: round records kept before the oldest are pruned (default 300)
